lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - A Listen and say. Then practise. Audio track 81,82

details: Listen and say checks understanding of word meaning and pronunciation of the food items. Practise allow students to repeat given words in a structured question and answer.
Look for careful listening, , clear pron of sports words, and confident repetition of the question and answer.
“I love sport! I play football after school. Do you play any sports?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - B. Ask and answer Audio track 83

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice using the target language to ask and respond to simple questions.Then moving on to personalised question and answer.
Look for use of ‘What does he/she do after school?’ questions, confident sentence answers with consistent reference to the sports and boy/girl  in the pictures. Then good speaking  in pairwork.
“Let’s find out what sports our friends play?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.69 - A Look and number

details: Look and number consolidates understanding of word–image connections. Students read words and look at visuals,  then show understanding by clearly writing the correct number.
Look for observation skills when viewing the visual, accurate choices of words for word recognition , and neat number writing in students’ books.
“Someone has left out all the sports equipment. Let’s figure out which sports they are for!”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.69 - B Cross out and write

details: Cross out and write tests their understanding of written words. Students read words then cross out incorrect letters. Finally they practise writing the words correctly inside lines.
Look for word recognition skills as they identity incorrect letters, then neat writing inside the lines given,

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.14 - Speaking Memory Game

details: The memory game reates semi-controlled practice for students in a fun way. They practise use of question and answer related to sports.
Look for correct question and answer sentence structures, and accurate use of the third person.
“Now, let’s see who plays those sports. Can yuo help me find out? We can return the equipment to them.”
